sources.notes: THERE IS NO STRUCTURED COURSE-WEBSITE OR SYLLABUS FIELD IN ANY TERM. Every course page links the same three things at course level: 'Course in Catalog' (the catalog SUBJECT page, e.g. catalog.illinois.edu/courses-of-instruction/cs), 'List of Terms offered' (/schedule/terms/S/N) and 'Register for Classes' (go.illinois.edu/RegisterForClasses). Pages from 2004-2016 carry the same labels. Structured course-website links: 0 of 118 sampled pages and 0 of 3,034 swept pages. URLs appear only as free text inside Section Info or the course description. 479 of 3,034 courses (15.8%) contain any URL, and almost all of those are about registration (go.cs.illinois.edu/csregister on 68 courses, go.illinois.edu on 188, queue/forms/waitlist/minor links). Only 19 courses (0.6%) carry a course-specific site or syllabus URL: BADM 372 practicum.web.illinois.edu; CHEM 444 nanogold.org; CS 124 cs124.org; CS 199 conversationalprogramming.org; CS 433 courses.grainger.illinois.edu; CS 466 el-kebir.net; CS 491 uiuc-cs491cap.netlify.app; ECON 198 go.economics.illinois.edu/syllabi; FSHN 120 publish.illinois.edu; IB 100 www.life.illinois.edu/bio100; MCB 150/151/250/251/252/253/354 www.life.illinois.edu/mcb/NNN (the one I tested, /mcb/150/, redirects to a generic MCB restrictions page); MCB 199 publish.illinois.edu; MCB 493 app.mcb.illinois.edu. In the 79 recent samples (which include the graduate 598 courses) 4 had one (CS 124, MCB 150, CS 598, ECE 598). Hosts found in older terms: uofi.box.com, wiki.illinois.edu, cs598kkh2022.web.illinois.edu, elahe.web.illinois.edu, yxw.web.illinois.edu, dependenttyp.es, tandy.cs.illinois.edu, sites.google.com, cs.illinois.edu/academics/courses/CS598DEL. 9 courses mention 'syllabus' without linking one. Course Explorer is therefore only a pointer source. Two pointers lead to real public syllabus stores, listed below: ws.engr getsyllabus (reached via CS 598 and the Grainger index) and the ECON Box archive (reached via ECON 198). Files: scratchpad/syllabi/fall2026_all.jsonl, fall2026_urls.tsv (all 553 course+URL pairs with context), ce_fall2026_findings.json, samples_all.jsonl, and the scripts ce_probe.py, analyse_ce.py, classify_urls.py.

results.summary:
Course Explorer and the catalog hold no syllabus content. They matter only as pointers, and those pointers lead to four public syllabus stores.

I fetched all 3,034 Fall 2026 Course Explorer pages the planner covers (numbered 000-499; 169 subjects, 9,701 sections, all HTTP 200). I also sampled 118 pages from other terms back to 2004: 79 from Spring 2025 to Fall 2026 across 39 subjects, and 39 from 2004-2025. No term has a structured course-website or syllabus field: 0 of 118 samples and 0 of 3,034 swept pages. The only course-level links are 'Course in Catalog', 'List of Terms offered' and 'Register for Classes'. Per-section URLs redirect to the home page.

Syllabus facts Course Explorer does carry, as free text in Section Info:
- Day1Access textbook cost: 90 courses, $21.59-$171.78.
- Topic titles and paragraphs for special-topics courses: 227 courses.
- Format notes (online, asynchronous, proctored).
- Occasional exam-date notes.
- Course-site URLs written as plain text: 19 of 3,034 courses (0.6%). Of the 479 courses with any URL, most are registration links.

The catalog was fetched in full: all 195 subject pages from the sitemap, 9,443 course blocks. It has no syllabus or website links and only 41 plain-text URLs, none of them a syllabus.

Following Course Explorer's pointers found four public syllabus stores:
1. **Grainger Course Websites index** (https://courses.grainger.illinois.edu/). For Fall 2026 it lists 607 engineering and physics courses in 19 subjects; 226 have a syllabus link, and 158 undergraduate courses have one outside Canvas. Robots.txt disallows only /secure/ and /private/.
2. **Grainger syllabus file store** (https://ws.engr.illinois.edu/custom/getsyllabus.asp?id=N). It has no robots.txt and needs no login. Walking IDs 1823-4036 should yield about 1,260 PDF or DOCX syllabi from Fall 2023 to Fall 2026, named {SUBJ}{NUM}_{YYYY}_{Term}. The ones I checked have grading weights, exams, textbooks and weekly schedules.
3. **Economics Box archive** (reached from ECON 198 via go.economics.illinois.edu/syllabi). It holds 1,482 files from 2010 to Fall 2026. Robots.txt allows the folder listings but blocks the file bytes, so the user or the department would have to download them.
4. **MCB PDFs** (app.mcb.illinois.edu/courses/syllabi/{SUBJ}_{NUM}_syllabus.pdf). 61 undergraduate syllabi; robots.txt is empty.

Canvas syllabus links need a login, and the /cisapp/, /search/ and /cim/ paths are disallowed by robots.txt.

Everything is in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-michaelcrews-THE-ADVISOR/348fb0bb-ab76-4776-87e7-d82b0f1dae46/scratchpad/syllabi/:
- Fall 2026 sweep: fall2026_all.jsonl, fall2026_urls.tsv, ce_fall2026_findings.json
- Stores: hosts/grainger_index_fa2026.json, engr/probe50.tsv, econ/boxfiles.json
- Scripts: ce_probe.py, analyse_ce.py, classify_urls.py, cat_sweep.py, econ/boxwalk.py

I did not edit any file in the planner.

I swept all 750 in-scope undergraduate catalog courses in the 16 rubrics, from public sources only. The rubrics are AE, ABE, BIOE, CEE, CS, ECE, IE, SE, ME, MSE, NPRE, PHYS, TAM, ENG, TE and CHBE. "ISE" has no courses of its own; its department's courses are IE and SE. I never logged in and never used the user's Chrome. Fetches were serial per host, 0.9-1.2 s apart, with the TruBot user agent, and robots.txt was read on every host. WebSearch was unusable because the session had already spent its 200-search budget, so all discovery came from plain fetches and the Wayback CDX API.

Result per course (in labels.json):
- FOUND, a real syllabus with grading plus exams or assignments: 450/750 (60%).
- Master (ABET-style) syllabus only (topics, texts, goals, no grading): 77.
- Official description only: 201.
- No WebTools profile at all: 22.

Found by department:
- AE 30/44, ABE 17/31, BIOE 29/48, CEE 37/72, CS 52/102, ECE 83/124
- IE 21/26, SE 24/26, ME 25/46, MSE 41/49, NPRE 14/34, PHYS 35/50
- TAM 16/23, ENG 8/18, TE 18/23, CHBE 0/34

Three findings matter most:
1. There is a Grainger-wide syllabus repository at ws.engr.illinois.edu/custom/getsyllabus.asp?id=N. Its IDs are sequential, it needs no login, and ws.engr.illinois.edu has no robots.txt. A HEAD request returns the filename as "{SUBJ}{NUM}[_{SECT}]_{YYYY}_{Term}.pdf". I swept the full ID range: 1,221 live files covering 440 courses from Fall 2023 to Fall 2026. That includes 939 files for 306 in-scope courses. Nine of the files were downloaded at random; all nine had grading, exams, textbooks, topics and attendance.
2. Every Grainger rubric (plus ABE, CHBE and TE) has a course profile served by one uniform endpoint, ws.engr.illinois.edu/courses/item.asp?course={SUBJ}{NUM}. It gives the description, the course web-page URL, attached Documents (syllabus PDFs through getfile.asp) and, for ECE, CS, ME and TAM, master-syllabus fields.
3. The courses.grainger.illinois.edu portal indexes every course website and syllabus link for the current term. Public course sites are fetchable, while roughly 315 web-page links go to Canvas, which requires login.

Why the other 300 are not available:
- 199 were not on the Fall 2026 portal and have no repository file, so they were probably not taught from Fall 2023 on.
- 153 have no web page listed in WebTools.
- 81 have Canvas-only sites (login).
- 22 point to the retired Compass2g system.
- 4 point to wiki.illinois.edu, which no longer resolves.
- 7 are public sites rendered by JavaScript (Notion, cs124.org and similar), so there is no syllabus in the static HTML.
- A few link to Box, which robots.txt disallows.
- A course can have more than one of these reasons.

About 35 of the unfound courses have older syllabus pages archived on the Wayback Machine.

CHBE has none: its profiles have no web pages, and the rubric is not in the Grainger portal or repository.

All scratch files are in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-michaelcrews-THE-ADVISOR/348fb0bb-ab76-4776-87e7-d82b0f1dae46/scratchpad/syllabi/eng/:
- labels.json: every course, found or not, with source URLs and reasons
- items_parsed.json: the 750 parsed profiles
- getsyllabus_full.tsv and getsyllabus_sample.tsv: repository ID to filename, content type and size
- getfile_ids.tsv: all 1,300 Documents IDs
- portal_rows.json: the 1,087 portal rows
- cg_results2.jsonl, ext_results2.jsonl, sec_results.jsonl, past_results.jsonl, deep_*.jsonl: the course-site checks
- canvas_status*.tsv: which Canvas syllabus pages are public
- cdx_*.txt: Wayback listings
- pdfs/: the 9 sample syllabus PDFs

The planner directory was only read; no file there was changed.

results.summary:
I checked all 764 planner courses in the 15 subjects (MATH, STAT, CHEM, MCB, IB, BIOC, PSYC, ASTR, ATMS, GEOL, ESE, NEUR, CPSC, NRES, FSHN) against every public source I could find. 232 (30%) have at least one public syllabus: 210 directly and 22 through a cross-listed partner. The other 532 are labelled not public, with reasons. Per subject (found direct + via cross-list / total): IB 67/71, MCB 55/64, BIOC 5/7, MATH 50/65, STAT 16/31, ASTR 9/20, CHEM 9/44, NRES 10/83, CPSC 5/58, NEUR 3/18, ESE 1/45, GEOL 1/43, PSYC 1/95, ATMS 0/46, FSHN 0/74.

Three indexes carry most of it:
1. MCB's syllabus library at app.mcb.illinois.edu/courses/{level}: 80 current full-syllabus PDFs, mostly Fall 2025 to Fall 2026.
2. IB's library at app.sib.illinois.edu/courses/: 93 PDFs, 21 of them Fall 2026.
3. Math's master-syllabus index at math.illinois.edu/resources/course-topics-instructors: 46 planner courses. These are topics, hours and textbook only, dated 2010-2017.

Two media-ID walks turned up files whose linking pages are login-only now:
- Math /document/1..1241: 219 section syllabi for 38 MATH courses, 2020-2022, plus MATH 453 Spring 2026.
- Chemistry /document/1..4421: 80 General Chemistry policy and syllabus files for CHEM 101/102/103/105/199/202/204, 2019-2025.

STAT, ASTR, NRES and PSYC syllabi live only on instructor sites. I found them by reading 1,539 department profiles and following their personal-site links one hop (1,184 seeds, 105 sites with syllabus or course links). Two more small sources: the ATLAS course server (courses.las.illinois.edu; 4 hits in 1,528 probes, no 2026 terms) and www.life.illinois.edu directory indexes.

Why the rest are not public:
- PSYC, ATMS, GEOL/ESE, FSHN, CPSC and NEUR publish no syllabi anywhere public. Full crawls, profiles and PSYC's 1,650 media ids found none.
- ACES keeps CPSC/FSHN/NRES syllabi on file but does not publish them.
- Upper-level CHEM, most PSYC and most other current courses use Canvas, where about 0.8% of courses are public (2 of a 241-id sample).
- Math's term directories and NetMath went behind SAML in 2023.
- faculty.math.illinois.edu is firewalled from off campus.

Other checks:
- Course Explorer 'Section Info' is a free partial source for every section: format, exam timing and Day1Access cost (CHEM 232 $129.41). schedule.mjs fetches these pages but drops that text.
- Several MATH gaps are cross-listed with CS/ECE/PHIL courses, which another sweep may cover: 357=CS 357, 450=CS 450, 473=CS 473, 475=CS 475, 362=ECE 313, 439=PHIL 439.

How I crawled:
- I read robots.txt on every host. All 14 department hosts use the standard Illinois Drupal file (admin/search/user paths disallowed); app.mcb, app.sib and courses.las allow everything; Canvas disallows only /page_views/.
- I never logged in or bypassed a login, bot check or CAPTCHA. Box downloads (robots-blocked) and the bookstore's bot challenge were left alone.
- Pace was the house user agent at about 1 request per second per host. One exception: chemistry.illinois.edu got about 2 requests per second for roughly 25 minutes while two jobs overlapped.

Scratch outputs under /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-michaelcrews-THE-ADVISOR/348fb0bb-ab76-4776-87e7-d82b0f1dae46/scratchpad/syllabi/:
- las_sci/coverage.json: per-course status, source URLs and terms, built by las_sci/coverage.py.
- math/topics_index.json, math/documents.txt, chem/documents.txt: the Math index and the two media-ID walks.
- las_sci/appmcb_links.json, las_sci/appsib_pdfs.json: MCB and IB syllabus lists.
- las_sci/laswww_probe.txt, las_sci/canvas_sample.txt: ATLAS and Canvas probes.
- las_sci/profiles_*.json, las_sci/hop2_a.json, las_sci/hop2_math.json, las_sci/sitecrawl_*.json: profiles, one-hop results and site crawls.

Sweep: LAS social sciences, humanities and languages. 30 subjects, 1,636 undergraduate catalog courses from public/illinois/index.json. 635 of them are offered Fall 2026 and 1,245 were offered between 2024 and 2026. Every course was checked against every source below. The per-course verdict for all 1,636 courses (status, reason, best URL) is in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-michaelcrews-THE-ADVISOR/348fb0bb-ab76-4776-87e7-d82b0f1dae46/scratchpad/syllabi/las-hum/coverage.json.

RESULT FOR ALL 1,636 COURSES
- 43 have a current public syllabus (2023 or later). 40 of these are ECON.
- 21 have an older public syllabus.
- 173 exist only in Wayback captures, mostly 2000 to 2018.
- 52 are listed in Political Science's syllabus archive but need a UIUC Box login. Another 42 PS courses are almost certainly the same (unverified because Box throttled the checks).
- 142 have descriptions only: the History course guides, 2001 to 2017.
- 1,163 have nothing public. 75 of those are independent study, thesis or topics shells where no syllabus is expected; 1,088 simply have no public syllabus anywhere.

FALL 2026 OFFERINGS (635 courses)
- 28 current public syllabus
- 8 older public syllabus
- 90 archived only
- 36 descriptions only
- 38 PS login-only or unverified
- 435 none

BY SUBJECT: courses with any public syllabus / catalog total
AAS 3/46, AFRO 0/58, ANTH 30/130, CHIN 0/16, CLCV 11/36, CWL 4/103, EALC 3/56, ECON 40/43, ENGL 11/112, FR 11/48, GER 20/40, GLBL 1/37, GRK 2/10, GWS 1/87, HIST 13/173 (plus 142 description-only), ITAL 6/30, JAPN 4/14, KOR 11/12, LAT 4/11, LING 7/50, LLS 4/63, PHIL 3/66, PORT 3/12, PS 11/128 (plus about 94 login-only), REL 1/94, RHET 4/5 (EUI 2008-2011), RUSS 10/27, SLAV 0/13, SOC 2/54, SPAN 17/62.
Outside ECON, almost all of these are archived pre-2018 captures.

THE ONE LARGE PUBLIC, CURRENT SOURCE: the ECON Box archive
- 1,482 files covering Fall 2011 to Fall 2026.
- Covers 40 of 43 undergraduate ECON courses. The 3 missing are 397, 398 and 399, which are independent study.
- 20 of the 27 undergraduate ECON courses offered Fall 2026 already have their Fall 2026 syllabus posted.
- A 12-file sample of recent syllabi contains: grading weights 11/12, exams 12/12, exam dates 6/12, homework 12/12, projects 11/12, attendance 11/12, textbooks 10/12, weekly schedule 11/12, instructor 12/12, format 11/12. Weekly hours appear in 0/12.
- A second ECON source: economics.illinois.edu/document/{id} redirects to 416 PDFs (IDs 9 to 1143). 293 of them are ECON syllabi from 2019 to 2026.

POLITICAL SCIENCE
- The archive lists 770 syllabus links covering 105 of 128 PS courses, Spring 2016 to Spring 2026.
- Every link I could verify (477 of 477) redirects to the UIUC Box login. So this archive is an index of instructor, term and course, not a source of content.

NO ARCHIVE AT ALL
None of these department sites keeps a syllabus archive: English (its Syllabus Archive is instructor-only), Rhetoric, SOC, ANTH, HIST, PHIL, REL, LING, AFRO, AAS, LLS, GWS, GLBL, CWL, FRIT, Germanic, EALC, Slavic, Classics, Spanish and Portuguese.

HOW THE SWEEP WAS DONE
- Same-host crawls of 22 department sites (30 to 342 pages each). None has a sitemap.xml.
- Box enumeration.
- The ECON /document ID sweep.
- Wayback CDX queries on 51 current and legacy uiuc.edu department hosts.
- The faculty.las legacy host.
- A directory-to-personal-site sweep: 1,404 profiles, of which 258 link a website, 20 instructors post syllabi, about 55 syllabus files.
- The Moodle archive, Canvas, IDEALS, the Gen Ed example folder, Course Explorer.
- Web search was used until the session's shared 200-query budget ran out. Instructor syllabi on Drive, Dropbox or personal sites not linked from a department directory could not be searched for. This is the main residual gap, mostly Rhetoric and language sections taught by grad students.

CRAWL TRAPS
1. Box throttles anonymous shared-link traffic by returning HTTP 404, not 429. It starts after roughly 150 to 250 requests and lifts after about 8 minutes, so a 404 does not mean the link is dead. Keep a known-public canary link and back off when it 404s.
2. Python urllib got 404 on public Box file pages that curl fetched as 200. Use curl-like requests.
3. Box's download endpoint (/index.php?rm=box_download_shared_file) is disallowed by robots.txt. The only robots-clean way to get file content: the /s/ page (allowed) carries an anonymous preview read-token, and that token fetches public.boxcloud.com/api/2.0/files/{id}/content (that host has no robots.txt). No login and no user credentials are involved, but it is a bearer token, so decide whether that is acceptable before running it at scale. Box pages also carry meta noindex,nofollow.
4. In Wayback, PDF URLs captured as text/html are soft-404 error pages. Filter on mimetype. The Internet Archive also went "Temporarily Offline" (503) several times.
5. IDEALS returns 403 to the UA string "TruBot/1.0 (...)". It answered to "Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; TruBot/1.0; ...)".

- Scripts (bin/): boxlist.py enumerates Box folders; boxfetch.py downloads public Box files; boxcheck3.py is the throttle-aware Box link checker; sitecrawl.py; facsites.py; cdx.sh; coverage.py.
- docs/: sample downloaded syllabi.

results.summary:
SWEEP: the professional colleges (Gies, ACES, AHS, Media, iSchool, Education, FAA, Social Work, LER, Law, DGS/Exploration). I checked all 2,436 of their undergraduate catalog courses (planner index.json, levels 100-499) against every public source I could list completely.

RESULT:
- 27 courses (1.1%) have a full syllabus that is still live.
- 73 more (3.0%) have a full syllabus that survives only as a Wayback Machine copy.
- 22 (0.9%) have partial facts only: learning objectives, course flyers, or Law course descriptions.
- 2,314 (95.0%) have nothing public.
- Recency of the 100 courses with a full syllabus: 40 have one from 2024 or later, 31 from 2020-23, 27 from before 2020, 2 undated.

Per college (courses / live / Wayback-only / partial):
- Gies: 166 / 3 / 6 / 0
- ACES: 533 / 7 / 9 / 0
- AHS: 234 / 0 / 0 / 0
- Media: 200 / 1 / 0 / 0
- iSchool: 90 / 3 / 0 / 13
- Education: 209 / 3 / 3 / 0
- FAA: 930 / 10 / 47 / 7
- Social Work: 43 / 0 / 0 / 0
- LER: 16 / 0 / 8 / 0
- Law: 9 / 0 / 0 / 2
- DGS/Exploration: 6 / 0 / 0 / 0

The only substantial archive is Urban & Regional Planning: 383 syllabus files from Spring 2015 to Fall 2024, covering 50 of the 64 undergraduate UP courses. The department removed them from its live site, and 186 of the 191 FA20-FA24 files now return 404. The Wayback Machine still serves them in full.

Why the rest is dark:
- Every college site I crawled carries catalog data only. That is 3,112 non-news pages from 19 host sitemaps (3,068 returned 200), plus 146 iSchool course pages and a list of 212 Law course pages.
- Gies and Education course pages are filled from APIs whose records have no syllabus field.
- ACES keeps syllabi on file for course-substitution review but does not publish them.
- LER says current syllabi are shared in Illinois Box (login).
- In practice, syllabi live in Canvas behind login.

Canvas does serve public syllabi without login at /courses/{id}/assignments/syllabus when an instructor opts in. Of 600 random IDs between 55,000 and 75,440, 5 were public (0.8%), and only MUS 107 was in these colleges. Of 147 Canvas IDs the Wayback Machine had captured, 99 are still public, and 94 of those 99 are in CS, ECE, TE or IE.

HOW THE CHECK WAS DONE:
- robots.txt read for 36 hosts.
- Sitemaps walked, including Gies's gzip-without-header sitemap.
- The LER WordPress REST media list read in full (the only college WordPress host whose REST media list is open; 16 others return 403).
- One Wayback CDX 'syllab' filename query per host domain across 37 domains, plus prefix queries where the whole-domain query timed out.
- Live re-checks of every candidate URL.
- Binary search of the current maximum Canvas course ID.

GAPS I COULD NOT CLOSE:
(1) The WebSearch budget for the session (200/200) was used up early, so syllabi on non-Illinois hosts (sites.google.com, github.io) were not enumerated.
(2) The CDX filter only matches URLs containing 'syllab', so files named differently are missed.
(3) The paginated CDX walk of the whole education.illinois.edu domain (237 pages) was stopped after 23 pages because Wayback returned 503s. Narrower prefixes covered the paths where syllabi would sit (/docs/, /sites/, /files/, the old ed.uiuc.edu host).
(4) A full Canvas pass, about 75k requests or about 25 h at 1.2 s each, was not run; only the 600-ID sample was.

- Scripts: sitemaps.mjs, sitecrawl.mjs, fetch.mjs, cdx.sh, cdxpages.py, canvas_probe.py, livecheck.sh, probe.py, pdftext.py.
- The planner directory was not modified.

results.summary:
I searched the web for a syllabus for 152 of the 153 sampled courses; one course, FR 299, never got a query. Search found a public syllabus for only 21 of 153 (13.7%), and only 13 (8.5%) are from 2024-2026. Checking three Grainger hosts directly found 3 current syllabi that search missed. With those, 24 of 153 courses have a public syllabus (15.7%) and 16 have a current one (10.5%).

**The sample.** I took every 40th course in public/illinois/index.json: 153 courses across 100 subjects. By level: 17 at 100, 35 at 200, 30 at 300 and 71 at 400. By college: 71 LAS, 24 FAA, 17 Grainger, 13 ACES, 6 AHS, 5 Education, 4 Gies, 4 Media, 4 iSchool, 2 ROTC, and 1 each for Law, LER and Social Work. I ran one query per course, e.g. "<CODE> syllabus Illinois <title words>". I checked about 40 candidates by fetching them and reading the term, and read each host's robots.txt. I never logged in, used credentials, got past a paywall or CAPTCHA, or used Chrome.

**Results by level (search only).**

| Level | Any year | Current (2024-2026) |
|---|---|---|
| 100 | 1 of 17 (5.9%) | 1 (5.9%) |
| 200 | 2 of 35 (5.7%) | 2 (5.7%) |
| 300 | 4 of 30 (13.3%) | 2 (6.7%) |
| 400 | 14 of 71 (19.7%) | 8 (11.3%) |

**Results by college (search only, any year).**
- **Grainger:** 10 of 17 (59%). Adding the direct host checks brings this to 13 of 17 (76%).
- **ACES:** 2 of 13.
- **iSchool:** 1 of 4, and it dates from 2000.
- **LAS:** 8 of 71 (11%).
- **Nothing found (0 hits):** FAA 0/24, AHS 0/6, Education 0/5, Gies 0/4, Media 0/4, ROTC, Law, LER and Social Work.

Courses with Fall 2026 sections did a little better: 12 of 68 (17.6%) any year, 9 (13.2%) current.

Besides full syllabi, 5 courses had partial pages (a reading list, ensemble meeting times, a 2021 course flyer). Two had syllabi behind a Box login (PS 281, PS 351), and one link was dead (LAS 195, Drive 404).

**Hosts ranked by search hits.**
1. courses.grainger.illinois.edu, same server as courses.engr and courses.physics: 6
2. Faculty and lab homepages on illinois.edu subdomains: 4, all old
3. ws.engr.illinois.edu: 3, plus 1 dead legacy link
4. app.sib.illinois.edu: 2
5. math.illinois.edu: 2, generic department outlines
6. Personal domains: 2
7. app.mcb.illinois.edu: 1
8. github.io: 1
9. sites.google.com: 0 full (1 partial)
10. drive.google.com: 0 (1 link returned 404)
11. docs.google.com: 0 in the sweep, though 2 public Docs syllabi are linked from the Grainger index
12. uofi.box.com: 0 public (everything requires login)
13. publish.illinois.edu: 0

**Hosts that can be listed directly instead of searched.**
- **Grainger course-website index** (courses.grainger.illinois.edu, one page, current term only): 160 undergraduate courses with a public syllabus link for Fall 2026.
- **Grainger syllabus store** (ws.engr getsyllabus.asp, walk ids 740 to 4,100): about 1,145 files from Fall 2023 to Fall 2026, about 510 distinct courses, about 350 of them undergraduate. I read ids 740-1397 in full and sampled 40% of the rest; 83 ids timed out and need a retry.
- **Legacy Grainger file store** (ws.engr getfile.asp): about 240 files, free-form names, including some non-syllabi.
- **Integrative Biology app** (app.sib, one page): 93 PDFs, 72 of them modified 2024-2026.
- **Molecular & Cellular Biology app** (app.mcb, five pages): 58 PDFs, 54 modified 2024-2026.
- **Math department** (one page): 105 outline pages plus 10 PDFs, undated.
- **NetMath:** about 20 course pages.
- **ECE and CS department course pages:** 329 and 351 pages. These are outlines with topics and textbooks but no grading.

**Traps to handle in a crawler.**
- An empty courses.grainger course/term folder still returns 200 with a generated template page. In a sample of 71 Fall 2026 course sites, 46 were templates and 13 redirected to a login.
- About 9% of the Grainger syllabus store is Word files, so filtering on PDF drops them.
- Some current terms redirect to Notion pages that plain fetches can't read.
- Search engines rank old-term pages first.
- Cross-listed courses resolve only under the other code; CPSC 436's syllabus exists only as IB 451.

**Searching per course misses syllabi that exist.** Where the Grainger store and index show a syllabus exists, search missed 3 of 13 courses (MSE 401, TE 466, NPRE 247). It also tends to surface only one term per course.

**Estimate for searching every course.** Scaling the sample rate to all 6,110 courses:
- About 840 courses with a public syllabus of any year (95% CI about 560-1,240).
- About 520 with a current one (about 300-860).
- About 6,110 queries at one query per course, or about 18,300 using all three query forms.
- About 900-1,000 follow-up fetches to confirm term and date.
- At the 200-searches-per-session cap hit here, at least 31 session budgets for a single pass.

A better plan is to enumerate the hosts above first, which covers roughly 700-800 courses without searching (mostly Grainger, IB, MCB and Math). Then search only as a fallback for the rest, mostly the long tail in LAS, FAA, ACES, Education, Gies and Media. Most courses will be labelled "not publicly available". The usual reasons are that the syllabus sits in Canvas or behind a Box or Moodle login, or that it was never posted.

**Scratch files** are in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-michaelcrews-THE-ADVISOR/348fb0bb-ab76-4776-87e7-d82b0f1dae46/scratchpad/syllabi/:
- results.tsv: all 153 courses with status, URL, host and term.
- direct_hits.tsv: the finds from direct host checks.
- sample.json: the 153-course sample.
- ws_sample.tsv, ws_full.tsv, ws_step3.tsv, ws_parsed.json and ws_legacy.tsv: the ws.engr id walks.
- grainger_fa2026_index.json: the parsed Grainger index.
- cg_sites_class.tsv: the template-versus-real check on 71 course sites.
- sib_lm.tsv and mcb_lm.tsv: file dates for the IB and MCB PDFs.
- robots/: saved robots.txt files.

sources.urlPattern: https://canvas.illinois.edu/courses/{id}/assignments/syllabus  (id 1..~75,600 on 2026-09-27). Files linked from a public syllabus: /courses/{id}/files/{fid}?location=course_syllabus_{id}. JSON: /api/v1/courses/{id}?include[]=syllabus_body works without login only when the course itself is public (is_public).
sources.enumerate: Canvas course ids run in sequence. Without logging in, GET /courses/{id}/assignments/syllabus returns one of three answers. 404 means no such course. 302 to /login means the course exists but its syllabus is not public, so label it 'not publicly available: Canvas login'. 200 means the syllabus is public. On 2026-09-27, id 75400 returned 302 and ids 75600 and above returned 404, so the sweep should run from 1 to about 77,600 to catch new courses. That is about 77.6k requests; at 1.1 s apiece it takes about 23.7 h. I wrote a resumable sweep script but did not run it: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-michaelcrews-THE-ADVISOR/348fb0bb-ab76-4776-87e7-d82b0f1dae46/scratchpad/syllabi/lms-archives/canvas_id_sweep.py. Start with the 146 course ids the Wayback Machine has a 200 capture for (canvas_wayback_ids.txt); 99 of those are still public today. The public course index is switched off (/search/all_courses redirects to login), so there is no faster complete listing. Search engines are no help either, because every page carries noindex.
sources.robots: robots.txt contains only 'User-Agent: * / Disallow: /page_views/', so syllabus paths are allowed. Every page does carry <meta name="robots" content="noindex,nofollow">. sources.robots: web.archive.org/robots.txt returns 404 (no file). archive.org/robots.txt disallows only /control/ and /report/. The Internet Archive's developer page on bots and automated access (https://archive.org/developers/bots.html) welcomes automated use under conditions: a descriptive User-Agent that includes the AI model name, delays between requests, honouring 429 and Retry-After, and limited concurrency. It publishes no numeric rate. When I ran 3 heavy CDX queries at once I got Errno 60 timeouts and one Errno 61 'connection refused', so run one CDX request at a time with at least 5 s between requests. The live hosts' own robots.txt disallows only /secure/ and /private/.

Illinois Media Space (mediaspace.illinois.edu): robots.txt allows most paths and channels are public, but it holds lecture video only. The archive has just 3 tag pages matching 'syllabus', and there are no syllabus documents.
wiki.illinois.edu and netfiles.illinois.edu live: neither host answers (retired). The wiki content survives only in the Wayback Machine (listed under sources).

Course Explorer / Course Information Suite (CIS): courses.illinois.edu/robots.txt disallows /cisapp/, /cisdocs/, /pdf/ and /search/. The CIS XML has no syllabus, textbook or grading field (only sectionText, sectionNotes and meetings). I made one request to /cisapp/.../CS/225.xml before checking robots, and did not repeat it. The allowed /schedule/ HTML pages contain no syllabus or textbook links either.

CIM-C course proposals: the Provost's guidelines say every new-course proposal must attach a syllabus, which would make this the most complete official store. But catalog.illinois.edu/robots.txt disallows /courseadmin/, /cim/ and /courseleaf/, so this is off-limits.

Provost 'Course Syllabus Resources' (https://provost.illinois.edu/policies/policies/courses/guidelines-for-new-or-revised-courses/course-syllabus-resources/): lists required syllabus elements and offers a template. It creates no public-posting duty and no repository. The Provost WordPress REST API (/wp-json/) redirects to a login page, so I used the sitemap instead (343 pages, no syllabus collection).
CITL 'Creating a Syllabus' (citl.illinois.edu): guidance, checklists and templates only; no collection of real syllabi.

Gen Ed 'Successful Gen Ed Course Proposals' (gened.illinois.edu/faculty-staff/recertification-status/successful-proposals/): has proposal excerpts for about 18 courses (e.g. CS 124, GEOL 115, HIST 209). Its 'Example Syllabi Box Folder' (go.illinois.edu/GenEdSyllabusExamples, which leads to uofi.box.com/s/inzkxelttbhu4q2emyvsprp6i0sznuav) returns 404 without login, so it is restricted.

Open Syllabus: analytics.opensyllabus.org puts a Cloudflare challenge in front of even robots.txt (CAPTCHA, not bypassed), and the corpus is licensed, not public. galaxy.opensyllabus.org (robots allows everything) shows only assigned-title counts, not syllabi.
Course Hero / Studocu uploaded syllabi: behind login and paywall, and their robots.txt disallows /api/, /search/ and /file paths.

Existing UIUC data repos have no syllabi. wadefagen/datasets (no licence field) holds gpa, course-catalog, geneds, graybook and teachers-ranked-as-excellent. illinois/prerequisites-dataset has no licence. EchoQuebec/UIUC-Course-Explorer-Data (MIT) is CIS XML. coatless-rpkg/uiucdata (GPL-3.0) holds grades and enrollment. sahansk2/uiuc_course_terms_dataset has no licence.
Illini Union Bookstore (for textbook and cost facts): bookstore.illinois.edu serves a JavaScript fingerprinting bot wall even on robots.txt, so it cannot be used without bypassing bot detection.
results.summary:
The LMS side is almost entirely behind login. Only a small, findable set of syllabi is public.

**Canvas (canvas.illinois.edu).** robots.txt disallows only /page_views/, but every page carries meta noindex,nofollow; the user should decide whether that matters for showing this content in the planner. Anonymous GET of /courses/{id}/assignments/syllabus has three outcomes: 404 means no course, 302 to /login means the syllabus is private, 200 means it is public. Ids run from 1 to about 75,600, so a complete sweep is about 77.6k requests, or about 23.7 h at 1.1 s. I wrote the script (lms-archives/canvas_id_sweep.py) but did not run it. Random samples found 5 public syllabi among 898 existing course shells. Seeding from the Wayback Machine worked well: one CDX call listed 1,619 archived Canvas course ids, 146 of them with a 200 capture. 99 of those are still public today, covering 29 catalog courses from Fall 2021 to Fall 2026 (CS, ECE, TE, MATH, IE, INFO, IS). Page titles encode term and code as 'Syllabus for Fall 2026-MATH 213-...'. Linked syllabus files were viewable without login in the one case checked. Expect roughly 60-150 catalog courses from a full sweep.

**Learn@Illinois (Moodle).** Only course summaries are public, and there is no robots.txt. 8,138 courses (mostly FA20-SP24) are listed through term-code searches, but only 8 summaries are syllabus-like. Course content redirects to login.

**Compass 2g, PrairieLearn, wiki.illinois.edu and netfiles.** Retired or entirely behind login. Media Space holds video only.

**Wayback Machine.** web.archive.org has no robots.txt. The Internet Archive's bots page welcomes automated use if you send a descriptive UA that includes the model name, add delays, honour 429/Retry-After and keep concurrency low. I got timeouts and one 'connection refused' when running 3 heavy CDX queries at once, so use 1 request at a time with 5 s or more between them.
- Grainger course hosts: 1,371 syllabus-named URLs covering 132 catalog courses, and 5,233 archived course-term site roots covering 698 catalog courses.
- Other hosts: math.illinois.edu 415 syllabus URLs (including the 2010-2015 Bourbaki/Syllabi pages); retired wiki.illinois.edu 88 URLs across 25 catalog courses; publish.illinois.edu 2,081 sites, about 71 of them course sites; legacy uiuc.edu hosts about 1,000 URLs.
- A complete archive pass means paging through 19,617 (illinois.edu) plus 7,493 (uiuc.edu) CDX index pages with the syllabus filter, about 4-5 days at a polite rate. A 43-page sample projects about 1,800 syllabus-named URLs (low confidence).

**Coverage.** Across everything in this sweep, 242 of the planner's 6,110 catalog courses have syllabus evidence, and 774 if the archived Grainger site roots count.

**Datasets and official stores.** No public UIUC syllabus dataset exists; GitHub has only about 15 single-course repos, mostly MIT/BSD/CC0. The one complete official store is CIM-C, where every new-course proposal must attach a syllabus, but catalog.illinois.edu's robots.txt blocks it. The Provost and CITL pages offer requirements and templates only. The Gen Ed example-syllabi Box folder is restricted.

**Process notes.**
- I made one request to the disallowed courses.illinois.edu/cisapp/ path before checking robots.txt, and did not repeat it.
- The shared scratch folder syllabi/ is also used by other agents in this run. I moved all my files into /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-michaelcrews-THE-ADVISOR/348fb0bb-ab76-4776-87e7-d82b0f1dae46/scratchpad/syllabi/lms-archives/ so they don't collide; key outputs are canvas_live_public.json, canvas_cdx_all.txt, cdx/*.txt, wayback_coursehost_sites.json, wiki_course_spaces.json, moodle_search_all.json and coverage_by_source.json.
- All background crawls are stopped.
- I edited nothing in the planner.

plan.pipeline:
LOCATION AND HOUSE RULES
- Put everything in scripts/illinois/syllabi/ as plain .mjs files, so both the system node 20.16.0 and /opt/homebrew/opt/node@23/bin/node (v23.3.0, used by dev.sh and build-index) can run them.
- Use the house user agent unchanged: 'TruBot/1.0 (+https://trumizzou.com; student project; respects robots.txt)'. For web.archive.org only, append ' syllabi/1.0', and when an agent runs the script, the model id (for example '(claude-opus-5-5)'), because the Internet Archive's bot page asks for that.
- Never spoof the user agent. A 403 to the truthful agent means do not crawl (IDEALS is an example).
- Never send cookies. Never follow a redirect into a login host: canvas.illinois.edu/login, shibboleth, saml_login, auth/saml2sso, uofi.account.box.com, login.microsoftonline.com. Record the redirect as 'login'.

FILES
- lib/http.mjs: the house get() pattern (3 tries with 3 s and 6 s backoff, 40-60 s timeouts). It adds:
  - a per-host queue: one request in flight per host, spacing = max(1,100 ms, robots Crawl-delay);
  - host aliases, so courses.grainger, courses.engr and courses.physics share one bucket;
  - at most 4 different hosts in parallel;
  - redirect: 'manual', so login redirects are seen and not followed;
  - 429/Retry-After handling, pausing a host after 3 consecutive 429 or 503 responses;
  - a HEAD mode for ID walks.
- lib/robots.mjs: RFC 9309 parsing (longest match, * and $), rules for 'TruBot' first and then '*', cached per run.
  - 404 or 410 means allow all.
  - Any other 4xx, any 5xx, or a redirect to a login means disallow all. This is stricter than the RFC.
  - Every URL's decision goes to data/syllabi/state/fetchlog.jsonl.
  - Meta robots nofollow (Canvas, Box) is also recorded, and links on those pages are not followed.
- lib/cache.mjs: a content-addressed raw cache at data/syllabi/raw/{host}/{sha256(url)[0,2]}/{sha256}.body, with a .json beside it holding url, finalUrl, status, content-type, content-disposition, last-modified, etag, fetchedAt and bytes.
  - Resumable: a URL already in the fetchlog is skipped unless --refresh is given or it is older than its source's TTL (stores 30 days, Canvas 120 days, Wayback never).
  - Refetches send If-None-Match / If-Modified-Since.
- lib/catalog.mjs: loads index.json (codes, titles, twins), offerings.json (terms, renumbered) and sections.json.
- sources/{id}.mjs: one file per registry entry. Each exports { id, hosts, enumerate(ctx) }, which yields candidates { source, url, kind: syllabus|outline|pointer|index, codeHints, termHint, sectionHint }.
- seeds.json: the hand-listed pages.
- hosts.json: the subject-to-department-host table used for the CDX, directory and Drupal /document/ steps. It must include hosts for the 66 unswept subjects, each confirmed by fetching the host root with the real user agent.
- pdftext.py: the text helper (see pdfTool).

STAGES (run.mjs --phase N --source ID; each stage's output is the next stage's input)
1. enumerate.mjs writes data/syllabi/candidates/{source}.jsonl.
   - ID walks store the highest live id, so a new term walks only the new range.
   - The researchers' id lists (getsyllabus_full.tsv, getfile_ids.tsv, math/documents.txt, chem/documents.txt, econ-documents.txt, canvas_wayback_ids.txt, cdx/*.txt) can seed the first run. Copy them out of /private/tmp now.
2. fetch.mjs fills the cache.
   - Every candidate: robots check, per-host pacing, fetchlog entry with the robots decision.
   - Stop a source when it fails 5 times in a row, and report it. Never let it write an empty result.
3. text.mjs writes data/syllabi/text/{sha}.txt plus {sha}.pages.json (character count per page).
   - PDF: pdftext.py (PyMuPDF, then pypdf as fallback).
   - DOC, DOCX, RTF: /usr/bin/textutil -convert txt -stdout.
   - XLSX and images: skipped and labelled.
   - HTML: remove script, style, nav and footer; turn block tags into newlines; turn table rows into tab-separated lines so grading tables survive; decode entities as courses.mjs does.
   - Canvas: only div#course_syllabus.
   - Google Docs: the /export?format=txt body.
   - Chunk nothing; keep the full text locally.
   - QA flags:
     - A page under 100 characters is 'image-only' (no OCR is available).
     - HTML text under 500 characters is 'js-shell'.
     - The courses.grainger fallback page is 'template'.
     - A login page body is 'login'.
     - Judge by extracted text length, never by the HTTP 200.
4. classify.mjs sets kind to full, outline, description, flyer, not-syllabus, js-shell, template or login.
   - It scores signals: a grading section with weights or points; exam, homework or assignment words; instructor or office hours; a schedule, week or date table; textbook or materials.
   - 'full' needs a grading signal and at least 2 others.
   - 'outline' has topics and texts but no grading. Lab reports and handbooks become 'not-syllabus'.
5. parse.mjs extracts facts deterministically, with evidence.
   - First, segment the text by headings from a lexicon: grading, grade breakdown, evaluation, assessment, course grade, exams, midterm, final, textbook, required materials, course materials, attendance, participation, schedule, tentative schedule, calendar, weekly topics, workload, expectations, format, delivery, labs, projects.
   - Grading: in the grading section (or the whole text if there is none), match 'label ... NN%' and 'NN% ... label' pairs, and points ('label ... NNN points' with a stated total). Map each label to a category (exams, midterms, final, quizzes, homework, labs, projects, papers, presentations, participation, attendance, discussion, other) and keep the original label.
     - Accept a set only if the percents sum to 98-102, or the points sum to the stated total.
     - Otherwise grading is uncertain, and the reason is kept (for example 'sum 85').
     - Handle 'drop lowest N', 'best of' and 'replace' as modifiers, not as weights.
   - Exams:
     - count Midterm/Exam/Hour exam N and number words ('two midterms', '3 one-hour exams');
     - final: yes, no or cumulative;
     - CBTF or proctoring;
     - dates: month-day patterns within 60 characters of 'exam', resolved to the document's term year;
     - conflicting counts make the field uncertain.
   - Workload: '(\d+)(?:\s*(?:-|to|–)\s*(\d+))?\s*hours? (?:per|a|each) week', 'weekly work hours', 'expect to spend'. Keep only values between 1 and 40.
   - Assignments, labs and projects: counts from numbered items or schedule rows; homework cadence (weekly, biweekly).
   - Attendance: graded if it has a weight, required, tracked (iClicker, sign-in), not required, or unknown; plus the number of allowed absences.
   - Textbooks: lines in the materials section containing an ISBN-10/13, 'edition', or an 'Author, Title' pattern; required or optional; 'no textbook', 'free', OER, open-access. Materials cost from Day1Access in Course Explorer Section Info.
   - Topics by week: rows starting 'Week N', or date-led rows in a schedule section. Keep at most 16 rows, each topic at most 80 characters.
   - Format: in-person, online, hybrid or asynchronous, plus lab or discussion. Take it from the syllabus, or from Course Explorer when the syllabus is silent, and say which.
   - Instructor: 'Instructor(s):' lines; cross-checked against the Course Explorer instructor surnames for the same term.
   - Every field carries { value, method: 'rule:<name>', evidence: page and character offset, confidence: high|medium|low }.
   - Publishing rule: publish high and medium; send low and all conflicts to 'uncertain'; never publish a number that does not appear in the text.
   - Optional --llm pass (the repo already depends on @anthropic-ai/sdk) only for 'full' documents where the rules failed on grading or exams. It returns JSON that is accepted only if every number and label occurs verbatim in the text and the weights sum to 100±1. Such fields are marked method 'llm-verified'.
6. match.mjs assigns course code, term and section.
   - Code, in order of precedence:
     1. the store's own key: the getsyllabus or getfile filename, app.mcb/app.sib filename, UP and ECON filenames, the Canvas page title, the Box listing name;
     2. the URL path: /{subj}{num}[{sec}]/{fa|sp|su}{yyyy}/;
     3. codes in the first-page header matching \b([A-Z]{2,4})\s?(\d{3})\b and present in index.json, ranked by frequency.
   - Renumbered courses: map old codes through offerings.json 'renumbered'. Accept a pre-2004 or renumbered hit only if its title overlaps the catalog title (token Jaccard 0.3 or more).
   - Cross-lists: a document naming several codes ('CS 374 / ECE 374', 'IB 451 / CPSC 436 / ENVS 420') maps to each of them. A document naming one code is propagated to its twins with via: 'cross-list of X'.
   - Multi-course pages (MUSC Electric Strings, math sections) map to each code with multi: true.
   - Topics shells (CS 498, ECON 490, PS 300, HIST 200) are attached per topic title and never shown as the course's general syllabus.
   - Graduate codes (500 and up) are dropped and counted.
   - Term, in order: the store key (filename _YYYY_Term, Canvas title, URL term directory), then the most frequent '(Fall|Spring|Summer) 20YY' on page 1, then PDF CreationDate/ModDate mapped to the upcoming term (July-November is fall, December-April is spring), then HTTP Last-Modified. Record which evidence was used; the last two give low confidence.
   - The course's 'best' document is the newest term with kind 'full', live before archived, whole course before one section. Every other document is listed as 'others' with its term, section, URL and source.
7. build.mjs writes three outputs.
   a) public/illinois/syllabi.json, containing only facts and URLs, never full text:
      { source, generatedAt, sources:[{id,name,url,robots,documents,courses}], courses:{ 'CS 225': { status, best:{url, source, term, section, instructor, kind, archived, fetchedAt}, facts:{grading:{components:[{label,category,weight}],basis,confidence}, exams:{midterms,final,cbtf,dates,confidence}, workload:{hoursPerWeek:[min,max]}, assignments:{homework,labs,projects,quizzes}, attendance:{policy,weight,allowedAbsences}, textbooks:[{title,authors,edition,isbn,required}], materialsCost:{amount,source}, format, topics:[{week,topic}]}, uncertain:[...], others:[...], via } } }
      - status is found, archived, partial, login-only or none.
      - Caps: 200 characters per string field, about 2 KB per course. No policy paragraphs are copied.
   b) public/illinois/syllabi-coverage.json has one row for every catalog course: status, a reason code, the list of source ids checked, and the best URL if any. Reason codes:
      - found-current, found-older, archived-only, partial-only;
      - login-only:{canvas|box|moodle|shibboleth};
      - not-offered-since-fall-2024 (1,128 catalog courses are absent from offerings.json);
      - no-syllabus-expected (the 361 shells);
      - js-only-site, retired-host (wiki, compass2g), robots-disallowed, unreachable (faculty.math);
      - no-public-source (the default, backed by the checked list).
   c) data/syllabi/coverage.tsv, a readable copy of the coverage file.
   - build-index.mjs can then fold each course's facts into public/illinois/course/{SUBJ}.json, so a detail card loads them with its shard and first paint does not load about 2 MB.
8. verify.mjs writes checks and sample sheets. Its checks load the published JSON the way the app loads it, because the planner's harnesses are not trusted.
   - Sample sheets go to data/syllabi/verify/{source}.tsv.
   - Invariants:
     - weights sum to 98-102;
     - exams per course 0-8;
     - no term later than the current term;
     - every code is in index.json;
     - every URL returned 200 when fetched, or is a web.archive.org id_ URL;
     - no field over 200 characters;
     - every catalog course has a coverage row;
     - the fetchlog has zero robots-disallowed fetches;
     - no source's document count drops more than 10% from the previous run (the collapse guard);
     - generatedAt moves forward.

.gitignore LINES TO ADD (I did not edit the repo)
data/syllabi/raw/, data/syllabi/text/, data/syllabi/state/, data/syllabi/manual/, data/syllabi/candidates/, data/syllabi/verify/. The two public JSON files and coverage.tsv are build outputs and can be committed.
plan.runPlan:
BUILD ORDER, then RUN ORDER. Wall times assume 1.1 s per host, hosts in parallel (up to 4), and 5 s between CDX calls.

0. Foundation (half a day of coding, no requests).
- Write lib/http, lib/robots, lib/cache, lib/catalog, text.mjs, pdftext.py and a first classify.mjs and parse.mjs.
- Tune them offline on the roughly 230 syllabi already downloaded in the scratchpad: eng/pdfs (9), las_sci/mcbpdf (72), las_sci/ibpdf (77), chem, math, las-hum/docs, and the 2 Google Doc exports. The fast feedback loop comes before any slow crawl.
- Do not ingest the 13 ECON files in las-hum/docs: they came through the Box preview-token route.
- Copy the researchers' id lists and caches out of /private/tmp before it is cleaned.

1. Index sources (~1 h wall, ~1,000 requests).
- grainger-index, ce-section-info (reuse cached pages), hist-guides, app-sib, math-topics, app-mcb, small-seeds, ischool, eui, moodle, stat-docs, ler REST, github, ps-box-index.
- After this phase, hand-check: 10 random documents from app-sib and from app-mcb, 10 math-topics pages, and 10 Section Info rows.

2. Grainger stores (~2 h wall, ~11,000 requests).
- The ws.engr bucket runs in sequence: getsyllabus HEAD walk 1-4,400 (81 min), getsyllabus GET 1,221 files (~25 min, about 250 MB), item.asp and list.asp (~16 min), getfile HEAD 1-1,300 plus 267 GETs (~29 min). About 2.5 h in all.
- In parallel: the courses.grainger bucket (sites, Physics template; ~70 min) and the external instructor hosts.

3. Text, parse and match on everything so far.
- About 3,500 PDFs through PyMuPDF takes about 4 minutes; parsing takes minutes.
- Hand-check 10 random documents per source: getsyllabus (stratified by term and file type, including 3 DOCX), getfile, courses.grainger, Physics, and external sites.
- Fix the rules and rerun. This loop is local and costs no requests.

4. Drupal media walks (~1.5 h wall, ~11,000 requests, one host each, in parallel).
- chemistry 1-4,800 (88 min), economics 1-1,400 (26 min), math 1-1,550 (28 min), stat 1-450 (8 min), psychology 1-1,650 (30 min; known to hold no syllabi, run once so it counts as checked).
- Probe /document/ on every other Drupal department host in hosts.json (a handful of ids each) to find more stores.

5. Directories and instructor sites (~2 h wall, ~7,000 requests).
- Rerun the LAS profiles. Add the professional colleges and the 66 unswept subjects. Take one hop to personal sites, with robots checked per host.

6. Wayback (~6-8 h, ~3,700 requests, one request at a time).
- About 130 per-host CDX queries (~1.5 h).
- About 3,500 id_ snapshot fetches at 3-5 s (3-5 h), including the UP archive, LER, faculty.las, publish, web.illinois and the 2 newest Grainger roots for each still-missing course.
- The Canvas CDX seed plus about 360 live checks (7 min).
- On a 503 'Temporarily Offline', back off 60 s and retry up to 5 times.

7. Manual ECON Box step (whenever the user has time).
- The user downloads https://uofi.box.com/s/1c1mp95oj255ekfkb1f9v01673yfbkzz and https://uofi.box.com/s/phtknm1rofcoisyphh5esbow0reqk58j in a browser into data/syllabi/manual/econ-box/. The pipeline lists the folders (about 50 requests, 3 s apart, with a canary for Box's 404 throttling) to attach Box URLs.
- Hand-check 10 of those files.

8. Canvas full id sweep (~24 h in the background, ~77,600 requests).
- Newest window first: ids 77,600 down to 40,000 takes about 11.5 h; the rest takes about 12 h. It is resumable.
- Hand-check every public page that maps to a catalog code, plus 5 private redirects, to confirm the 302 detection.

9. Web search fallback (multi-session).
- About 1,990 Fall 2026 non-shell courses with nothing, at 200 searches per session, is about 10 sessions. Record 'searched: no public result' as the reason.

10. Optional deep passes.
- Wayback domain-wide CDX (27,110 pages, 4-5 days).
- Canvas ids below 40,000.
- ATLAS brute-force probes for fall2021-fall2024 (764 per term).
- A headless render of the 7 JS-only public sites, in a local headless browser, never the user's Chrome.

TOTALS: phases 1-6 are about 34,000 requests and about 13-15 h of wall time. The Canvas sweep adds about 24 h. Search adds about 10 sessions.

EVERY TERM
- Grainger index; getsyllabus and getfile above their stored highest ids; app.sib; app.mcb; Math topics; the ARCH flyers while their term is live; the new Canvas id window (about 5-7k ids, 2 h); Course Explorer Section Info.
- Re-verify best URLs with conditional GETs.
- Make the scrape part of the planner's regular build, so the data does not silently go stale.

VERIFICATION
- Code and term matching: for every source, 10 random documents (all of them if fewer), roughly 300 documents in total. Target at least 98% correct code and term.
- Field accuracy: a hand-labelled gold set of 150 documents, stratified as 100 PDF, 15 DOCX, 25 HTML and 10 Canvas. For each field, measure precision and recall of the published values. Target at least 95% precision on grading weights, exam count, final yes/no, textbook ISBN or title, and format. Report recall; expect 60-80% for grading. Fields below target stay 'uncertain' until they are fixed.
- Invariants run in verify.mjs on every build (listed in the pipeline).
- Coverage completeness: 6,110 rows, each with at least one checked source. The 770 formerly unswept courses must show their subject's host in the checked list.
- In-app check through the in-app browser: 5 course cards (CS 225, IB 150, ECON 102, UP 101, PSYC 100). Confirm the facts, term, source link and 'no public syllabus: reason' text render.
plan.pdfTool:
Checked on this machine on 2026-09-27.

The planner's node_modules has no PDF library. There is no pdfjs-dist, no unpdf and no pdf-parse. It also has no HTML parser (no cheerio, parse5, htmlparser2 or jsdom); undici is the only relevant package.

On the system:
- No pdftotext, pdfinfo (poppler), mutool, qpdf or tesseract. `brew install poppler` would add pdftotext if wanted.
- /usr/local/bin/python3 (3.14.3) has PyMuPDF 1.28.2 (`import pymupdf`), pypdf 6.9.2, pdfplumber 0.11.10, pdfminer.six 20260107 and bs4 4.14.3. It does not have python-docx or lxml.
- macOS's built-in /usr/bin/textutil converts .doc, .docx, .rtf and .html to text: `textutil -convert txt -stdout FILE`.

Benchmark on 49 real syllabus PDFs from the scratchpad (9 Grainger, 20 MCB, 20 IB):

| Library | Total | Per PDF |
|---|---|---|
| PyMuPDF | 3.3 s | 0.07 s |
| pypdf | 30.1 s | 0.6 s |
| pdfplumber | 205.9 s | 4.2 s |

No PDF lacked a text layer.

pdfplumber is the house precedent: scripts/illinois/excellent-teachers.mjs calls it through execFileSync and finds an interpreter via the PYTHON env var or a list of python3 candidates.

Recommendation: a helper, scripts/illinois/syllabi/pdftext.py, that uses PyMuPDF for per-page text, falls back to pypdf when PyMuPDF throws, and uses pdfplumber only for table extraction on pages with a grading heading. Find the interpreter the same way excellent-teachers.mjs does.

Time for about 3,500 PDFs:
- PyMuPDF: about 4 minutes.
- pypdf alone: about 35 minutes.
- pdfplumber for everything: about 4 hours.

PyMuPDF is AGPL-3.0. That is fine as a local build tool whose output is facts. If the user prefers permissive licences only, pypdf (BSD) is the default.

Pages under about 100 characters are flagged as image-only and their facts marked uncertain, because no OCR is installed.

The system node is v20.16.0; dev.sh and build-index use /opt/homebrew/opt/node@23/bin/node (v23.3.0). Write the scripts as plain .mjs with no type stripping.
plan.summary:
I merged the seven sweeps into one registry of 32 deduplicated public sources, ranked by courses per request. I measured coverage against the planner's real catalog and wrote a build and run plan for scripts/illinois/syllabi/. I did not edit the planner. My only web traffic today was 5 requests: Box's robots.txt and 4 HEAD requests to the Grainger syllabus store.

**What a public syllabus scrape can find today.** I merged every sweep's per-course verdicts into scratchpad/syllabi/design/merged_coverage.json, built by design/merge.py. Cross-listed "twins" from index.json inherit a found syllabus.
- **Whole catalog:** of 6,110 courses (all numbered 000-499), 753 (12.3%) have a current full syllabus (Fall 2023 or later). 1,166 (19.1%) have a full syllabus of any age. 244 have only partial facts, 93 exist only behind a login, and 4,607 have nothing.
- **Fall 2026 offerings:** of 3,034, 495 (16.3%) are current and 696 (22.9%) have any full syllabus.
- **Grainger:** 62% current, 72% of its Fall 2026 courses. Grainger has instructors upload syllabi to a public store.
- **LAS:** 8.4% current. IB, MCB, MATH and ECON are strong; PSYC, ATMS and FSHN are near zero.
- **Other colleges:** FAA 0.8% current (7.1% any, mostly the archived Urban Planning files), ACES 5%, Gies, Education, Media and iSchool 0.5-2%. AHS, Social Work, ROTC, Vet Med and Law have 0 current.
- **By level:** 400-level is best at 17%; 200-level is worst at 6.6%.

**After the full pipeline I expect:**
- about 780-900 courses current (13-15%);
- about 1,230-1,380 with any full syllabus (20-23%);
- for Fall 2026: 17-19% current and 24-26% any.

**Why most courses will say "not publicly available".** Canvas holds most syllabi, and about 99% of Canvas courses are private. Box folders need a login (Political Science, English, Rhetoric). ACES keeps syllabi on file but does not publish them. Many department sites dropped their files around 2018.

**Where the value is.** The top sources:
- The Grainger index: 1 request points to about 160 public syllabi.
- The Grainger file store at ws.engr.illinois.edu: 1,221 files for 317 courses, 208 of them found nowhere else. Walking it takes about 1 h 45 min.
- The Integrative Biology and MCB libraries: about 143 courses for about 230 requests.
- The Math topic index: about 65 courses, topics and textbooks only.
- The History course guides: 155 courses, descriptions only.
- Course Explorer's Section Info notes: materials cost, format and exam timing for every Fall 2026 section, at no new requests. schedule.mjs already fetches those pages but throws this text away.
- Wayback per-host queries: about 317 courses whose only syllabus is an archived copy.

The full Canvas course-id sweep is last. It takes about 24 hours and should add only 5-40 new courses: of the 27 catalog courses already known to have a public Canvas syllabus, only INFO 102 had no other source.

**The pipeline.** It runs in eight stages: enumerate, fetch, text, classify, parse, match, build, verify.
- **Crawling:** it uses the house TruBot user agent and a 1.1 s pace per host, with host aliases so courses.grainger, courses.engr and courses.physics share one queue. Robots rules are enforced and logged for every URL. Login redirects are recorded, never followed.
- **Raw cache:** data/syllabi/raw is resumable, and it must be added to .gitignore along with the text, state, manual, candidates and verify folders.
- **Text extraction:** a Python helper using PyMuPDF, with pypdf as fallback. Word files go through macOS textutil.
- **Facts:** parsing is rule-based, with evidence and a confidence level. Grading is shown only when the weights sum to 98-102. Nothing is published unless it appears verbatim in the text; low-confidence results go to an "uncertain" list.
- **Matching:** course and term come from filenames, Canvas titles and URL term folders before the document text. Cross-lists use index.json twins, and renumbered courses use offerings.json.
- **Outputs:** public/illinois/syllabi.json holds facts and the source URL only, never full text. public/illinois/syllabi-coverage.json gives every course a status, a reason code and the list of sources checked.

**Run order.** Build and tune the parsers first on the roughly 230 syllabi already downloaded in the scratchpad. Then run: index sources (about 1 h), the Grainger stores (about 2 h), the department document walks (about 1.5 h), directories and instructor sites (about 2 h), Wayback (6-8 h), the manual ECON step, the Canvas sweep (about 24 h), and web search over what is left (about 10 sessions).

**Verification.** Hand-check 10 documents per source for course and term (target 98%). Build a 150-document hand-labelled set for field accuracy (target 95% precision on published fields). Invariants run on every build, including zero robots-disallowed fetches and a guard against any source's count dropping more than 10%.

**What "100%" can honestly mean.** Every course gets checked against every public source that can be listed, with a reason recorded. Every file in those sources gets captured. It cannot mean a syllabus for every course, finding syllabi on personal sites or drives that nothing links to (search is capped at 200 per session), current syllabi everywhere, or anything behind a login.

**Issues you should know about:**
- scripts/illinois/excellent-teachers.mjs already downloads from a Box path (/index.php) that Box's robots.txt disallows. I re-checked the file today.
- One researcher fetched 13 ECON files through Box's preview token, which gets around that same rule. Those copies should not be used.
- One researcher hit the disallowed /cisapp/ path once, and another ran chemistry.illinois.edu at about 2 requests per second for about 25 minutes.
- No researcher swept 770 catalog courses in 66 subjects (CMN, GGIS, AFST, ETMA, MDVL and others). The pipeline covers them through its host table.

**Decisions for you:**
- Whether to download the two public ECON Box folders yourself. They are the only current source for 16 ECON courses, including 102, 103, 202 and 203, and the bot cannot fetch them without breaking Box's robots rules.
- Whether to spend about 24 hours on the Canvas sweep.
- Whether republishing facts from Canvas and Box pages marked noindex,nofollow is acceptable.
